newsitem.title: USA: Cummins says Q3 hurt by truck engine slump.
newsitem.headline: Cummins says Q3 hurt by truck engine slump.

text.p: Cummins Engine Co Inc said its third-quarter results reflected a "continuing decline in sales of heavy-duty and midrange truck engines."
The decline, which was expected, was offset by higher sales to power generation and industrial markets, it said.

The company reported third-quarter net earnings of $26 million, or $0.67 per share, on sales of $1.3 billion. This compares with third-quarter 1995 net earnings of $46 million, or $1.14 per share, on sales of $1.2 billion.
Shares in Cummins were off 7/8 to 40-3/4.

Sales of $274 million to the heavy-duty truck market were 24 percent lower than a year ago and 11 percent lower than the second quarter of 1996, Cummins said. Midrange truck engine sales were eight percent lower than a year ago and 13 percent lower than the second quarter, the company said.
Sales of $166 million for the bus and light commercial vehicle market were 19 percent higher than the third quarter of 1995 and 14 percent lower than the second quarter of 1996.

Power generation sales of $348 million were 29 percent higher than the third quarter of 1995 and 12 percent higher than the second quarter of 1996. "All of the increase was experienced in international markets, due primarily to strong demand in China, India and Southeast Asia," it said.

Sales to industrial markets were level with the second quarter of 1996 and were 23 percent above the third quarter of 1995, due to strong sales of engines for construction equipment in international markets, Cummins said.
Sales of filtration products and turbochargers were $133 million, essentially level with the prior year, it said.
